verses.text: When the time came near for David to die, he gave these instructions to his son Solomon:
"I am about to go the way everyone on earth must go. So be strong and act like a man.

Do what the LORD your God tells you. Walk in his ways, and keep his laws, commands, rules, and teachings, as they are written in the Law of Moses. Then you will do well in everything you do and wherever you go.

And the LORD will keep the promise he made to me. He said, 'If your descendants are careful to live faithfully before me with all their heart and soul, you will always have a man on the throne of Israel.'

You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me. He killed the two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them in a time of peace as if it were war, and their blood splashed on the belt around his waist and on the sandals on his feet.
Deal with him in your wisdom. Do not let him grow old and go down to the grave in peace.
But be kind to the sons of Barzillai from Gilead. Let them eat at your table, because they helped me when I ran away from your brother Absalom.

And remember Shimei son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, who is with you. He put a terrible curse on me on the day I went to Mahanaim. But when he came down to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised him by the LORD, 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'
But now do not let him go unpunished. You are wise, and you will know what to do to him. Make sure he dies a bloody death in his old age."
Then David died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David.
David had ruled over Israel for forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was made very secure.
Then Adonijah son of Haggith went to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. She asked him, "Have you come in peace?" He answered, "Yes, in peace."
Then he said, "I have something to say to you." She said, "Go ahead."
He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine. All Israel expected me to be king. But things changed, and the kingdom went to my brother, because the LORD gave it to him.
Now I have one thing to ask of you. Please don't refuse me." She said, "Go ahead."
He said, "Please ask King Solomon to give me Abishag from Shunem to be my wife. He won't say no to you."
Bathsheba said, "All right. I will speak to the king for you."

So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king stood up to meet her and bowed down to her. Then he sat down on his throne and had a throne brought for the king's mother, and she sat at his right side.
She said, "I have one small thing to ask of you. Please don't refuse me." The king said to her, "Ask, my mother. I will not refuse you."
She said, "Let Abishag from Shunem be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife."

King Solomon answered his mother, "Why are you asking for Abishag from Shunem for Adonijah? You might as well ask for the kingdom for him too! After all, he is my older brother, and Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah are on his side!"
Then King Solomon made a promise by the LORD: "May God punish me, and even more, if Adonijah does not pay with his life for asking this!
The LORD has made me secure on the throne of my father David and has given me a royal family, as he promised. So as surely as the LORD lives, Adonijah will be put to death today!"
So King Solomon gave orders to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck Adonijah down, and he died.

Then the king said to Abiathar the priest, "Go back to your own fields in Anathoth. You deserve to die, but I will not put you to death now, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD for my father David, and you shared in all the hardships my father went through."
So Solomon removed Abiathar from being the LORD's priest. This made the LORD's word come true, which he had spoken at Shiloh about the family of Eli.
When the news reached Joab, he ran to the LORD's holy tent and took hold of the horns of the altar. Joab had supported Adonijah, although he had not supported Absalom.
King Solomon was told, "Joab has run to the LORD's tent and is standing beside the altar." Then Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go and strike him down."

Benaiah went into the LORD's tent and said to Joab, "The king says, 'Come out!'" But Joab answered, "No, I will die here." Benaiah went back to the king and told him, "This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me."
Then the king said to Benaiah, "Do as he says. Strike him down and bury him. Then my father's family and I will no longer be blamed for the innocent blood Joab spilled.

The LORD will pay him back for the blood he spilled. Without my father David knowing it, he attacked and killed two men who were better and more honest than he was: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army.
May the guilt for their blood be on Joab and his descendants forever. But may the LORD give peace forever to David, his descendants, his family, and his throne."
So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and struck Joab down and killed him. He was buried at his own home in the wilderness.
The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada in charge of the army in Joab's place, and he put Zadok the priest in Abiathar's place.
Then the king sent for Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Do not go anywhere else.
On the day you leave and cross the Kidron Valley, you can be sure that you will die. Your blood will be on your own head."
Shimei answered the king, "That is fair. Your servant will do what my lord the king has said." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.
But three years later, two of Shimei's slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Shimei was told, "Your slaves are in Gath."
So Shimei got up, put a saddle on his donkey, and went to Achish at Gath to look for his slaves. He went and brought his slaves back from Gath.
Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had come back.

So the king sent for Shimei and said to him, "Didn't I make you promise by the LORD? Didn't I warn you, 'On the day you leave to go anywhere else, you can be sure that you will die'? And you said to me, 'What you say is fair. I will obey.'
So why did you not keep your promise to the LORD and obey the command I gave you?"
The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your heart all the evil you did to my father David. Now the LORD will pay you back for your evil.
But King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will be secure before the LORD forever."
Then the king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. So the kingdom was made secure in Solomon's hands.
